name: Sennacherib
bio:
Sennacherib, king of Assyria, invaded Judah in Hezekiah's fourteenth year, capturing all its fortified cities. Hezekiah tried to buy him off, stripping the temple and palace of silver and even gold from the temple doors to pay the tribute Sennacherib demanded, but Sennacherib still sent his officers Tartan, Rabsaris, and Rabshakeh with a large army to besiege Jerusalem itself. Rabshakeh, speaking for Sennacherib, mocked Hezekiah's trust in both Egypt and the LORD and warned the people on Jerusalem's wall that no god had ever saved a nation from Assyria's hand (2 Kings 18:13-35).

## 📖 Core Story: Defeat and Assassination

Hearing that Tirhakah, king of Ethiopia, was marching to fight him, Sennacherib sent Hezekiah a second letter full of boasts and threats, warning that no god could save Jerusalem from Assyria as none had saved other nations. Hezekiah prayed over the letter in the temple, and the prophet Isaiah delivered the LORD's blistering response: Sennacherib's pride and blasphemy against the Holy One of Israel would not go unanswered; he would not even shoot an arrow into Jerusalem, but would return home the way he came. That night the angel of the LORD struck down 185,000 men in the Assyrian camp. Sennacherib withdrew to Nineveh, where, while worshipping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his own sons Adrammelech and Sharezer assassinated him with the sword and fled to Armenia; another son, Esarhaddon, succeeded him as king (2 Kings 19:8-37).
